name: SplinePath
src_typeComment: The shared, re-editable path/spline core: a list of points authored in this object's LOCAL space (so moving or rotating the object moves the whole path), evaluated as a Catmull-Rom curve via SplineUtils. Genuinely independent of PathBuilder — drop this alone on an object with SplineFollower for a patrol path, a camera path, anything that just needs to move something smoothly through hand-placed points. PathBuilder additionally requires one of these on the same object to generate prefabs/meshes along it.  Edited via the Scene view: select this object (or a PathBuilder on the same object) to get click-to-add / drag-to-move / click-to-remove point editing — see PathBuilder/Editor/SplinePathSceneEditing.

src_serialized.name: points
src_serialized.tooltip: Points along the path, in this object's LOCAL space. Edit via the Scene view (Ctrl+Click to add, drag to move, Alt+Click a point to remove) or directly here.

src_serialized.name: tension
src_serialized.tooltip: 0 = a smooth curve through every point (standard Catmull-Rom). 1 = dead-straight segments between points, still passing through every one. In between loosens/tightens how far the curve bulges past a straight line.

src_serialized.name: lengthSamplesPerSegment
src_serialized.tooltip: Samples per segment used when measuring the path's length. Higher is more accurate but slower to rebuild. Rebuilt automatically only when points/tension/transform actually change, never per-frame.

src_members.sig: public float Tension { get => tension; set { tension = Mathf.Clamp01(value); InvalidateCache(); } }
src_members.name: Tension

src_members.name: SetLocalPoint

src_members.name: InsertPoint

src_members.sig: public Vector3 EvaluateWorld(float t) => transform.TransformPoint(SplineUtils.Evaluate(points, t, tension))
src_members.name: EvaluateWorld
src_members.comment: Evaluates the path in WORLD space at t in [0,1].

src_members.sig: public Vector3 EvaluateTangentWorld(float t) => transform.TransformDirection(SplineUtils.EvaluateTangent(points, t, tension))
src_members.name: EvaluateTangentWorld
GetLength
src_members.comment: Total path length in WORLD units (the length table is built from world points, so this stays correct under any transform scale/rotation rather than only being right when the object is unscaled).

src_members.name: GetPointAtDistance
src_members.comment: Returns the WORLD position at a given distance along the path (0 = start, GetLength() = end; clamped outside that range). This is what makes constant-speed following and even prefab/mesh spacing possible — see SplineFollower and PathBuilder.
